channel.description: The FOX News Rundown is your daily news podcast for making sense of the big issues directly impacting your life. Go beyond the headlines every morning and join some of FOX News’ most exceptional journalists—including FOX News Channel reporters Peter Doocy, Aishah Hasnie, Bill Melugin, Alex Hogan, Lucas Tomlinson and Jacqui Heinrich and FOX News Radio reporters Dave Anthony, Jessica Rosenthal, Lisa Brady, and Gurnal Scott - as they tap into the global reporting resources of FOX News and get unparalleled political analysis and exclusive insight from top newsmakers. The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders on 2028 and What the GOP Got Wrong in 2026
item.description:
Republicans are trying to regain their footing after losing their majorities in the House and Senate, while looking ahead to 2028. Arkansas Republican Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders joins the Rundown to break down what went wrong for the GOP, while also looking ahead to the 2028 presidential field. She also discusses her new book, Unapologetic: Clarity and Conviction in a World Gone Crazy.
Before the Pilgrims ever landed in America, they fled a ruthless era of absolute monarchs where believing differently than the king was considered treason. Historian and bestselling author William J. Federer joins FOX News correspondent Lucas Tomlinson to reveal the history behind the first Thanksgiving, the Mayflower Compact’s role in self-government, and how presidents from George Washington to FDR helped shape the holiday.
PLUS, commentary by Rich Zeoli, host of The Rich Zeoli Podcast.

item.title: The National Dog Show Returns with a Record Number of Dogs Competing
item.description:
This year's 'National Dog Show' marks the silver anniversary of the show, featuring about 2,100 dogs competing for 'Best in Show' and introducing three new breeds, including the Russian Balanca and Teddy Roosevelt Terrier. The show airs 'Thanksgiving Day', Thursday, November 26, 2026, at noon ET. The show's longtime host returns for his 25th year and joins the podcast to tell us why he looks forward to this every November.
FOX's Gurnal Scott speaks with John O'Hurley, actor, tv personality and longtime host of the 'National Dog Show', who shares his favorite moments he looks forward to every year, and how much the show is connected to great causes for dogs.

item.title: Scandal Forgotten? President, Wall Street Cheer NVIDIA CEO’s Return
item.description:
Just 11 days after resigning, Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of NVIDIA, sparking a massive Wall Street rebound after last week’s brutal tech selloff. FOX Business contributor and Black River Management Chief Market Strategist Lou Basenese joins The Rundown to discuss the whirlwind corporate drama. They break down the behind-the-scenes pressure from shareholders, tech leaders, and President Trump to bring Huang back, while warning that major questions remain about Huang’s ability to lead—as well as lingering national security concerns.
Thanksgiving travel is seeing its first year-over-year decline since the pandemic, with AAA estimating 81.5 million Americans will travel this holiday week. That is a 0.1% dip—roughly 120,000 fewer travelers—compared to last year. While higher gas prices and economic concerns may be keeping some people home, recent airport outages and air traffic control issues could also have travelers rethinking their plans. AAA Northeast Senior Public Affairs Manager Robert Sinclair Jr. joins The Rundown to talk about what’s behind the dip, how ongoing flight disruptions and a potential nor’easter could impact holiday travel, and what to expect heading into the busy Christmas season.
PLUS, commentary by David Marcus, columnist for FOX News Digital. 
PHOTO CREDIT: AP IMAGES

item.title: A Massive Driver’s License Scheme in Florida — and the Questions It Raises
item.description:
An undercover scheme at a Florida DMV allegedly gave hundreds of illegal immigrants driver’s licenses, and now officials are auditing whether any of them voted in razor-thin elections. A whistleblower exposed the partnership between a local driving school and a rogue DMV employee as the Trump administration cracks down on illegal immigrants obtaining commercial driver’s licenses.FOX’s Eben Brown speaks with Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia about the scheme, the revocation of licenses, ongoing election integrity audits, and why Florida’s elections were tighter than expected.

item.title: Is China Getting Its Hands on America’s Most Advanced Technology?
item.description:
With Republicans preparing to hand over control of the House in January, what can still get done before the end of the year, and what challenges lie ahead for the next Democrat-led Congress? House Intelligence Committee Chairman Rick Crawford (R-AR) joins the Rundown to discuss the GOP’s remaining legislative priorities, including government funding, the farm bill and the National Defense Authorization Act. Crawford also addresses growing bipartisan concerns over China’s access to advanced American technology, and the push to reauthorize a key foreign surveillance program.
The rising cost of healthcare sees many Americans paying more for their health insurance premiums, raising the simple question — why? Yale University Associate Professor of Public Health and Economics Zack Cooper joins the Rundown to break down why employer based health coverage is going up as lawmakers question a program widely advertised as “Medicare for All.”
PLUS, commentary by Tevi Troy, senior fellow at the Ronald Reagan Institute and a former senior White House aide. Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

item.title: How to Handle Politics at the Thanksgiving Table & New Year Goals with Vanessa Van Edwards
item.description:
As we prepare to gather with loved ones this Thanksgiving, the holiday comes with a side of tension and disagreement for many of us. Even with a long, bitter election season behind us, some political wounds still haven’t healed.
Earlier this week, behavioral researcher Vanessa Van Edwards joined Alex Hogan to share research-backed strategies for navigating heated political conversations around the Thanksgiving dinner table and building stronger connections in a divided climate. Van Edwards broke down how to set ground rules, spot "emotion words" before a discussion goes off the rails, and pivot back to common ground. She also shared rapid-fire advice on conveying confidence, making friends as an adult, sticking to New Year’s goals, and turning small talk into meaningful stories on screen and in person.
The conversation was full of helpful advice, but it was too long to fit into our regular midweek Rundown. So, on today's FOX News Rundown: Extra, we'll let you hear the whole conversation with Vanessa Van Edwards and more of her great tips for holiday dinners and other parts of your life.
